cmd_update_app_failed_cli_stays: Atlas Desktop could not be updated, so Atlas CLI stays on v{version}
cmd_update_app_failed_no_rollback: Atlas Desktop could not be updated and the CLI could not be rolled back ({reason}). The CLI is v{version}; run `atlas desktop --install` to bring the app to it.
cmd_update_bad_tag: The release tag "{tag}" is not a version Atlas understands
cmd_update_channel_alpha_audience: Contributors and testers who accept breakage in exchange for the newest work.
cmd_update_channel_alpha_cadence: Whenever the maintainer cuts one, often several times a week.
cmd_update_channel_alpha_promise: The default while Atlas is in alpha. Fresh builds cut straight from main, with little soak. Features can be unfinished and behavior can change between builds.
cmd_update_channel_alpha_risk: Expect rough edges and breaking changes
cmd_update_channel_alpha_switch: You get the newest build of any channel, so a settings or config change may not be readable by an older Atlas. Going back to Beta or Stable later waits for a newer build there, or you can reinstall it explicitly.
cmd_update_channel_beta_audience: People who want next release's features a few weeks early and will report what breaks.
cmd_update_channel_beta_cadence: A new beta about every one to two weeks while a release is soaking.
cmd_update_channel_beta_promise: Feature-complete builds that are being soaked before they become Stable. Only fixes land between betas.
cmd_update_channel_beta_risk: Mostly works; a bug can slip through
cmd_update_channel_beta_switch: You get the newest beta or release candidate, and Stable as soon as it is newer. Going back to Stable later waits for a Stable newer than your build, or you can reinstall Stable explicitly.
cmd_update_channel_missing: The channel {channel} is missing from the list of channels. Run `atlas update channel` again.
cmd_update_channel_pick: Pick a channel [1-3 or name, {@common_os_enter_key} keeps {selected}]:
cmd_update_channel_pick_invalid: Enter 1, 2, 3, stable, beta or alpha, or nothing to keep {selected}.
cmd_update_channel_save_failed: Couldn't save the update channel to {path}
cmd_update_channel_stable_audience: Anyone who uses Atlas for real work and wants only soaked builds.
cmd_update_channel_stable_cadence: When a soaked beta is promoted, usually every few weeks.
cmd_update_channel_stable_note: While Atlas is in alpha, Stable means soaked through alpha and beta, not finished.
cmd_update_channel_stable_promise: Only builds that already ran as a beta, with nothing changed since but the version number.
cmd_update_channel_stable_switch: You move to the next Stable release that is newer than the version you run. Atlas never installs an older build by itself.
cmd_update_check_failed: Couldn't check for updates. Check your network connection (it needs curl).
cmd_update_describe_ahead: You run v{installed}, which is newer than what {channel} offers (v{offered}).
cmd_update_describe_ahead_nothing: Nothing is installed: you will get updates again when the {channel} channel passes your build.
cmd_update_describe_unrecognized: Nothing installable on the {channel} channel (unrecognized tag '{tag}').
cmd_update_desktop_could_not_follow: Atlas Desktop could not follow: {reason} (not fatal). Run `atlas desktop --install`.
cmd_update_dev_build: This atlas is a dev build or linked to one ({path}). `atlas update` only replaces release installs; run `atlas unlink` to go back to the release build.
cmd_update_downgrade_needs_confirmation: A downgrade needs your confirmation and there is no terminal to ask in. Run it in a terminal, or pass `--yes`.
cmd_update_downgrade_not_newer: `--downgrade` only applies when the {channel} channel offers an older build than v{current}, and v{offered} is newer. Run `atlas update`.
cmd_update_downgrading: Downgrading v{current} → v{offered} ({channel}). Data written by v{current} (settings, caches, terminal host state) may not be readable by the older build; back up `~/.atlas` first if it matters.
cmd_update_exit_runner_old: The runner keeps the old version until you run: {command}
cmd_update_hint_linked: atlas v{version} is available (running a linked/dev build; `atlas update` skipped)
cmd_update_host_check_error: Terminal host check failed: {reason}. Run `atlas hostd --check`.
cmd_update_host_check_failed: Terminal host check failed ({status}). Run `atlas hostd --check`.
cmd_update_installed_by: Installed by {manager}: `atlas update` downloads, verifies and installs the package.
cmd_update_linked: atlas is linked to a dev build ({path}). Run `atlas unlink` first.
cmd_update_lock_busy: Another Atlas update is already running. Wait for it to finish.
cmd_update_no_exe: Couldn't find the running atlas binary
cmd_update_offer_downgrade: {tag} (older than v{installed}: nothing is installed unless you ask)
cmd_update_package_download: Install the v{version} package for your distribution: {url}
cmd_update_package_unknown_manager: Installed by a system package, but no package manager (pacman, dpkg, rpm) was found.
cmd_update_pkg_auth_cancelled: Authentication was cancelled. Nothing was installed.
cmd_update_pkg_auth_unavailable: pkexec could not authenticate (is a polkit authentication agent running?). Nothing was installed.
cmd_update_pkg_confirm_or_run: Installing a system package needs your confirmation. Run it in a terminal, pass `--yes`, or run: {command}
cmd_update_pkg_empty_command: There is no install command to run
cmd_update_pkg_needs_confirmation: Installing a system package needs your confirmation and there is no terminal to ask in. Run it in a terminal, or pass `--yes`.
cmd_update_pkg_needs_terminal: Installing a system package needs a terminal, or pkexec for the password. Run it in a terminal: {command}
cmd_update_pkg_no_escalation: Neither sudo nor pkexec is available to install the package as root. Install one of them, or run the install command as root.
cmd_update_pkg_will_run: This installs v{version} with {manager} as root:
cmd_update_stage_note: Atlas is in alpha. Every channel, including Stable, can have rough edges and breaking changes until the first release that meets the general availability criteria in the versioning policy.
cmd_update_switched_downgrade: Offers {tag}, which is older than what you run; nothing changes unless you run {command}.
cmd_update_switched_none: It offers nothing right now (or Atlas is offline).
cmd_update_switched_same: Offers {tag}: that is what you run.
cmd_update_tarball_empty: The atlas binary in the tarball is empty, so Atlas does not install it
cmd_update_tarball_missing: Couldn't find the atlas binary in the tarball
cmd_update_unwritable: Can't update, nothing was changed: {blocked}. Fix the permissions, or reinstall into your home folder with the shell installer (`sudo atlas update` would leave files owned by root there).
cmd_update_yank_none: No {channel} release that is not withdrawn is published yet.
cmd_update_yank_rollback: The newest {channel} release that is not withdrawn is v{offered}, older than what you run: {command} installs it (settings written by v{installed} may not be readable).
